chunks: My father (RA) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from one of those who narrated from our scholars, from Abu Abdillah (AS) who said:
I heard him say: A servant is not an actor (doer of an action) unless he is capable, and he may be capable but not an actor, and he will never be an actor until capability is with him.

key_terms.فَاعِلًا: actor or doer of an action

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between human ability and action in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* articulates the Shia theological stance on *istita'ah* (capability), affirming that while human action necessitates concurrent capacity, the mere presence of capacity does not compel action, thereby preserving human agency. It underscores the distinction between the ontological possibility of an act and its volitional execution, a key point in debates against the Mu'tazila and Ash'ari schools regarding divine decree and human free will.
